title.narrative: Nourishing Hope: Integrated Food Security and Health project to promote resilience for the most vulnerable communities in Madaya

description.narrative: ltpgtAccording to the "Health Sector Syria Annual Report 2023" the number of people in need (PiN) of life-saving and life-sustaining assistance in Syria exceeded 15.3 million in 2023, reflecting a 13% increase from 2021. Of this population, 29% are women, 46% are children, 17% are persons with disabilities (PwD), and 4% are elderly. Approximately 4% of the affected population are pregnant women requiring pre- and post-natal care and safe delivery. The Syrian health system remains weak, fragile, and disrupted, further strained by concurrent public health emergencies, which significantly affect the accessibility, availability, and quality of health services across the country.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtAdditionally, Syria ranks as the sixth-highest country for food insecurity globally. The WFP estimates that 12.1 million Syrians—more than half the population—suffer from hunger, with another 2.9 million at risk of becoming food insecure, marking a 52% increase in just one year. Nutritional conditions are deteriorating, with rising rates of stunting and malnutrition in some regions.ltbrgtThe proposed project aims to deliver multi-sectoral assistance to the most vulnerable groups in Madaya, Rural Damascus, by establishing a Primary Health Care (PHC) center. This center will provide primary health services and integrate food assistance through a specific selection criteria using an E-Voucher system, ensuring service complementarity. This initiative aligns with Strategic Objective 1 (SO1): to support and strengthen the delivery of critical basic services to ensure the most vulnerable populations in underserved locations affected by conflict, displacement, and natural shocks receive integrated life-saving and life-sustaining humanitarian aid.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtProposed Activities Under the Health SectorltbrgtEstablishment of a PHC Center in Madaya:ltbrgtThe PHC center will be established in collaboration with the Syrian Arab Red Crescent (SARC) and will have:ltbrgtClinics: The center will include a gynecology clinic, a pediatric clinic, and an internal medicine clinic.ltbrgtMobile Team for Physiotherapy: A mobile team will provide physiotherapy services to people with disabilities and distribute assistive devices as a complementary activity.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtTraining: Specific training sessions will be conducted for the Department of Health (DoH) and SARC teams.ltbrgtThe PHC center will not only provide medical care but also act as a referral point for individuals identified as severely food insecure. Health workers will screen patients for food insecurity during routine health check-ups and refer severe cases, particularly among vulnerable groups and those with socio-economic challenges. The center will register all cases, incorporating questions to assess the economic situation and vulnerability profile of beneficiaries. PLWs and CU5 with malnutrition issues will be included in the selection criteria for referral to food assistance.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtFood AssistanceltbrgtThe food assistance component will support the most vulnerable cases based on data collected during PHC operations and nominations from community committees in targeted locations. The assistance will amount to $73 per cycle for 8 cycles, following recommendations from the FSA.ltbrgtBy integrating health and food assistance, the project aims to address both immediate and underlying needs of the most vulnerable populations in Madaya, enhancing their resilience and improving their overall well-being. The project will focus on the most vulnerable households (HHs), especiallyltbrgt Women-headed HH, HH with elderly, HH with PWD, HH with children under 5 years of age, HH with high number (more than 3 in the HH) of children, HH with PLWs. lt/pgtltpgtltspangtThe intervention is built upon TDH Italy's ongoing experience in FSA voucher assistance in several locations, health projects in Syria, and current e-voucher assistance in Rural Damascus. TDH's expertise in FSA is rooted in its previous nutrition, food security, and related projects, implemented with support from the lt/spangtltspangtSHF and other donors across southern and northern Syria.lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgt
